title: Long-Stay Mileage Records: Establishing the Included Miles a Keyturn Trip Booking Still Has Unused
content:
On a Keyturn Trip Booking that has been running for some time, the included miles the reservation still has unused are established from the reservation's own mileage record rather than from the unused figure standing on it, and on the longest-running reservations that record is brought up to the day.

1. Where the trip has run for at least 28 days, that is four weeks, and at least 3 odometer readings have been booked against the reservation, the miles still unused are worked out from the reservation's own mileage record, as the included miles granted to it less every mile its readings have booked against that allowance.
2. Where the trip has run for at least 28 days and fewer than 3 odometer readings have been booked against the reservation, the miles still unused are worked out from that same mileage record and are then reduced by the standard daily included-mile measure for each day that has passed since the latest reading.
3. In every other case the miles still unused are taken as the unused included miles standing on the reservation.

### What is counted, and how the days are counted

The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted. The days that have passed since a reading are counted from the day that reading was taken to the day of handling, the day of the reading not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The two conditions, in their combinations

| Days the trip has run | Odometer readings booked against the reservation | The miles still unused |
|---|---|---|
| 28 or more | 3 or more | The included miles granted, less every mile the readings have booked against that allowance. |
| 28 or more | Fewer than 3 (that is, 0, 1 or 2) | That same figure, reduced by the standard daily included-mile measure for each day since the latest reading. |
| Fewer than 28 | 3 or more | The unused included miles standing on the reservation. |
| Fewer than 28 | Fewer than 3 | The unused included miles standing on the reservation. |

Both limbs of the first two rows must hold together. A reservation that has run 27 days falls to the third row whatever its readings show, and a reservation that has run 28 days — the threshold being reached, not passed — falls to the first or second row according to its readings.

### Hypothetical readings of the ladder

*A trip that has been running 41 days with 5 odometer readings booked against it.* Both limbs of the first row hold. The reservation's mileage record shows 3000 included miles granted and readings that have booked 2600 miles against that allowance, so the miles still unused are 400.

*A trip that has been running 41 days with 2 odometer readings booked against it.* The second row governs. The same mileage record gives 400 miles, and that figure is then reduced by the standard daily included-mile measure for each day that has passed since the latest reading: where the latest reading was taken 3 days before the day of handling, 3 days of that measure come off the 400 miles.

*A trip that has been running 12 days with 6 odometer readings booked against it.* Neither of the first two rows holds, because the trip has not run 28 days. The miles still unused are the unused included miles standing on the reservation.
